questions.q: What purpose do unhappy chemicals serve?
a: They warn us of threats and push us to act
They erase memories of past pain
They balance out the happy chemicals exactly
They make social bonding possible
questions.why: Lesson 1 says unhappy chemicals protect us by warning of potential threats.

questions.q: Why does the modern brain trigger cortisol so often?
a: The neocortex sees danger everywhere, though real threats are rare
People today sleep less than their ancestors
Cortisol is released whenever we feel happy
Modern diets contain more stress hormones
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the rational neocortex spots risk around every corner, keeping us in alarm mode.

a: Getting used to things so they no longer bring the same joy
The habit of chasing new rewards daily
A chemical that blocks dopamine release
The brain's tendency to avoid all change
questions.why: Lesson 2 says experiences make us happiest when new, then fade as we adapt.

questions.q: Why does the author say permanent happiness is a myth?
a: Every pleasant experience fades as the brain adapts
Happiness depends mostly on income and status
Only some people are born with happy brains
The brain can only release so much dopamine
questions.why: Lesson 2 says even a lottery win would not end the happiness journey because of habituation.

questions.q: What does the author call the only real mistake in life?
a: Refusing to make a choice at all
Choosing the wrong option
Changing your mind too often
Letting your emotions guide you
questions.why: Lesson 3 says not choosing is the one decision that truly makes you unhappy.
